title: AI scraper 怎麼壓垮一個 wiki——cookmeplox 從 10× 流量、residential proxy、到 JA4 偵測的覆盤
summary: Weird Gloop 的 cookmeplox 把 Minecraft / OSRS / League wiki 一年來的 AI scraper 戰役寫成覆盤——對手散在數百萬支住宅 IP、偽裝成 Chrome 120、甚至繞 Google Translate 與 Facebook link preview；防線從 Cloudflare challenge 一路升到 JA4 指紋 + MediaWiki 行為 ML。真正吃資源的不是頻寬，是 cache miss 的 50-100 倍 CPU——95% server issue 都從這裡來。
widget_questions: What does each layer of the AI-scraper bypass stack (User-Agent spoofing, residential proxy pool, Google Translate proxy, Facebook link preview) defeat, and which mitigation specifically catches it?
How does the proportion of unusual-parameter requests, multiplied by the 50-100x cache-miss CPU cost, determine the effective compute multiplier that explains the 10x figure cookmeplox observed?

At each mitigation stage (Cloudflare challenge, UA+IP firewall, JA4/TLS fingerprint, MediaWiki behavioral ML), what fraction of scraper traffic does it catch, what bypass technique defeats it, and what is the lifetime before adversaries adapt?

Across four observed traffic classes (real Chrome user, residential-proxied bot, datacenter bot, Facebook/Google-laundered bot), which fingerprint dimensions (UA, ASN, JA4, MediaWiki behavior) actually disambiguate humans from scrapers and which dimensions are collapsed into the same cell?
What does a typical day's request rate look like when scraper bursts (1000+ req/s) interleave with the ~100 req/s human baseline, and how does the burst overlap with the European morning human peak?
